tytul: Honey-fermented garlic: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for garlic fermented in raw honey.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to Ask Extension, there are no research-based recipes that prove fermenting garlic in raw honey is safe, or that show how to do it safely.
Honey should not be fed to infants under 12 months of age: it is the one dietary source of Clostridium botulinum spores linked to infant botulism by both laboratory and epidemiologic studies.

K-State says fermenting garlic in raw honey is risky: garlic is a low-acid food, honey varies from low to high acidity, the water activity of the mixture is unknown, and botulism has occurred in garlic in oil.

akapity: According to an Extension expert, fermentation is not an approved, safe method of preserving garlic, and there are currently no validated recipes for fermenting garlic.
The FDA list gives garlic a pH of about 5.80.
Honey can also be a source of infant botulism in children under age one.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for garlic fermented in honey from a checked source.
